Writing side sums X,Y and pair weights x_i,y_i, any zero a_i forces Y-y_i≥2 and X+y_i≥2; any zero b_i forces X-x_i≥2 and Y+x_i≥2. For weight ≤3, a doubly zero pair forces X,Y≥2 (impossible), while no doubly zero pair forces total weight≥n≥5. At weight4 a doubly zero pair necessarily exists and X=Y=2. Zeros must then align on matched pairs, and each side sum2 leaves only one index carrying 2 on both sides or two indices carrying 1 on both. Both types satisfy the constraints. Independent enumeration over all 3^10 ternary labelings for n=5 restricted to weight≤4 found min4 and exactly15 minima; script proof covers arbitrary n≥5 independently of this test. n=4 excluded as stated.
